scenarios.title: Session chips in compact mode
scenarios.caption: The identical five sessions with session details turned off: chips shrink to a single line, fitting more of them in the same row.

scenarios.title: Update-available badge on the overflow control
scenarios.caption: After a background check finds a newer release, the 'More actions' control carries a single accent dot until the user opens About; its menu gains an 'Update to fesTerm 0.3.0…' entry above the usual items.

scenarios.title: Session chips with details shown
scenarios.caption: The same five sessions with 'Show session details in chips' enabled: each chip carries a secondary line under its title.

scenarios.title: Serial connect form
scenarios.caption: Serial launches ask only for a device path and line settings; there is no host/credential concept for a local serial device.

scenarios.title: SFTP connect form
scenarios.caption: The SFTP launch surface defaults to opening the graphical two-pane file manager once connected.

scenarios.title: SSH connect form with Advanced settings expanded
scenarios.caption: Expanding 'Advanced settings' reveals the port-forwarding controls beneath the always-visible connection, authentication and durable-session sections.

scenarios.title: SSH connect form
scenarios.caption: The default SSH launch surface: a Connection section led by the squashed user@host:port field and repeating it as Username, Host and Port, an Authentication section for the credential method, and the durable-remote-session toggle, with Advanced settings collapsed.

scenarios.title: Session Inspector over a durable tmux session
scenarios.caption: The same overlay for a session attached through fesTerm's durable persistence provider, showing the extra 'Durable session' facts and 'Resume' (rather than 'Reconnect') action.

scenarios.title: Session Inspector over an SSH session
scenarios.caption: The inspector overlay reporting connection facts and a pending host-key fingerprint for a plain SSH shell, without covering the terminal it describes.

scenarios.title: Compare, after the file changed underneath the editor
scenarios.caption: The conflict banner stays pinned above a read-only, line-oriented comparison of the unsaved version against the one the file now holds, so the choice is made with both versions in sight.

scenarios.title: A document's three states side by side on the chips
scenarios.caption: Saved, edited, and changed-underneath are three different shapes before they are three different colours, so the row still reads with the colour taken away.

scenarios.title: Closing the last view of a document with unsaved changes
scenarios.caption: Closing the only remaining view of a typed-in document asks before anything is lost, names the file and where it lives, and makes Save the action the keyboard already has hold of.

scenarios.title: Find and Replace over the open document
scenarios.caption: One regular-expression dialect for the toolbar and the command area alike, saying which match of how many is current before anything is replaced.

scenarios.title: The per-view editor options
scenarios.caption: Line numbers, a fixed column count and vi keys belong to this view alone: another window on the same file keeps its own, and none of them touches the text.

scenarios.title: The editor with the Markdown outline beside it
scenarios.caption: The same rail the Markdown viewer has, offered while the file renders as Markdown: the headings stay in reach without scrolling to find out where you are.

scenarios.title: A Markdown file as it opens
scenarios.caption: A Markdown document lands in Preview, reading as the finished thing; the mode control above it is the way back to the source.

scenarios.title: Choosing where a document is written
scenarios.caption: One destination browser for both origins, stating an overwrite in words before the fact rather than asking a second time after the Save is already pressed.

scenarios.title: The native editor, everything saved
scenarios.caption: A fictional project's notes open for editing, with the origin, the commands, and the status band the editor reports through.

scenarios.title: The editor split with its live preview
scenarios.caption: One view, two panes: the text on the left and the same document rendered on the right, so a Markdown change can be read as it is typed.

scenarios.title: Source coloured by what it means
scenarios.caption: Keywords, strings, numbers, types and comments are told apart by role rather than by language, from the same palette the Markdown preview's fenced code uses.

scenarios.title: The native editor holding unsaved changes
scenarios.caption: The same document after typing: the banner, the chip state, and the status band all report one unsaved document rather than disagreeing.

scenarios.title: The vi command area over the open document
scenarios.caption: One line above the persistent status bar, never in place of it: what the document is and where the caret sits stay readable while a command is being typed.

scenarios.title: A view with vi compatibility switched on
scenarios.caption: The view says which mode it is in, in words, above the text as well as in the status bar, so a letter behaving as a command is never a surprise.

scenarios.title: A vi search matching as it is typed
scenarios.caption: The same regular-expression dialect the Find bar uses, counting what Enter is about to accept rather than what was last run.

scenarios.title: Keyboard bindings editor, collapsed
scenarios.caption: Actions grouped by scope, each showing its current chord as keycaps; one customized action carries a 'Customized' badge.

scenarios.title: Keyboard bindings editor filtered by search
scenarios.caption: Typing into Search narrows the list to matching actions and hides scope groups with no match.

scenarios.title: Keyboard bindings editor capturing a chord
scenarios.caption: 'Record shortcut' arms live chord capture; the editor waits for a chord instead of dispatching whatever is pressed next.

scenarios.title: Keyboard bindings editor with an action selected
scenarios.caption: Selecting an action expands its inline editor directly under its own row, showing scope, default, and current chord as read-only context.

scenarios.title: Markdown workspace with the outline open
scenarios.caption: The heading outline docked alongside the document, letting a reader jump straight to a section of a longer file.

scenarios.title: Markdown workspace, rendered preview
scenarios.caption: A fictional project's Markdown fetched over an already-authenticated SFTP session, shown in rendered preview mode with headings, a list, and a code block.

scenarios.title: Markdown workspace, source mode
scenarios.caption: The same document toggled to raw source, for readers who want to see the Markdown itself rather than its rendering.

scenarios.title: New Session in the compact launcher-grid layout
scenarios.caption: The 'Compact New Session layout' preference shrinks the launch cards so saved profiles and running sessions start higher up the window.

scenarios.title: New Session on first run, before any profile exists
scenarios.caption: The empty/first-run state: only the fixed launch cards, with no saved profiles or resumable sessions panels to show yet.

scenarios.title: New Session at a narrow, responsive width
scenarios.caption: The same populated launcher reflowing at a narrow window: cards and panels stack instead of sitting side by side.

scenarios.title: New Session with saved profiles and running sessions
scenarios.caption: Launch cards sit above saved profiles of every kind plus resumable local, tmux, and screen sessions, at a normal desktop width.

scenarios.title: Profiles list
scenarios.caption: Every saved local, SSH, SFTP, and serial profile in a single searchable table, each row carrying an overflow menu for connecting, editing, duplicating, and deleting.

scenarios.title: Serial profile editor
scenarios.caption: Device path and line settings (baud, data bits, parity, stop bits, flow control) for a saved serial profile.

scenarios.title: SFTP profile editor
scenarios.caption: The same SSH-family editor in SFTP mode, offering the graphical file-manager toggle instead of a terminal type.

scenarios.title: SSH profile editor
scenarios.caption: Editing an existing SSH profile's connection metadata and durable- session settings.

scenarios.title: Settings: Interface and Scrolling
scenarios.caption: The top of Settings: chip layout, session-detail, and workspace-restore toggles, followed by scrollback limit and scroll-speed controls.

scenarios.title: Settings: Quick switch
scenarios.caption: The single toggle controlling whether held quick-switch modifiers overlay chip numbers.

scenarios.title: Settings: SFTP
scenarios.caption: Pane order and the default local directory used when opening new SFTP tabs.

scenarios.title: Settings: Terminal typography
scenarios.caption: Font family, programming ligatures, and emoji presentation, all scoped to terminal cell rendering only.

scenarios.title: The SFTP graphical file-manager workspace
scenarios.caption: Local and remote panes browsed side by side; the local pane lists an invented project directory, never the real filesystem.

scenarios.title: Copy and Paste in the terminal context menu
scenarios.caption: A selection remains visible while the terminal's context menu offers Copy and Paste alongside Find, without sending the secondary click to the remote program.

scenarios.title: Actions for a detected terminal path
scenarios.caption: Secondary-clicking a filesystem path freezes the detected target in the menu, where it can be opened in the editor or copied exactly as a path.

scenarios.title: The sftp command-line interface
scenarios.caption: The terminal-driven `sftp` client, distinct from the graphical file manager: directory listing, a `get`, and its transfer-progress line.

scenarios.title: A connected SSH terminal session
scenarios.caption: A remote shell mid-use: service status, a log tail, and the resting prompt, rendered by the same grid the terminal view paints for a real PTY.
